title: Goose Technical Search Integrity Rules
purpose: Catch high-confidence technical conditions that can block or weaken Search and AI discovery before longitudinal outcome evidence is mature. This is a non-composite diagnostic rule pack, not a ranking or AI-readiness score.

rules.claim: Google treats robots.txt 4xx responses other than 429 as if no robots.txt exists, while 429/5xx/network failures can temporarily suppress or reduce crawling.
rules.action: Fix robots.txt 429/5xx/network availability problems; do not misclassify an ordinary 404 as a Google crawl block.
rules.doesNotProve: A crawlable site will be indexed or ranked.

rules.claim: A robots.txt file can allow the site root while blocking specific priority paths. Google applies the most specific matching allow/disallow rule, with allow winning equal-length conflicts.
rules.action: Remove unintended path-specific Googlebot blocks from priority Search pages while preserving intentional private/utility exclusions.
rules.doesNotProve: That an allowed priority URL will be crawled, indexed or ranked.

rules.claim: Priority Search pages need a successful response and must not expose noindex when they are intended to be discoverable.
rules.action: Fix failed responses and unintended noindex directives on priority pages.

rules.claim: A supporting page for Google AI Overviews or AI Mode must be indexed and eligible to appear with a snippet; nosnippet and max-snippet:0 restrict that eligibility.
rules.action: Remove snippet-blocking directives only when Search/AI snippet visibility is actually desired.
rules.doesNotProve: Inclusion in AI Overviews or AI Mode.

rules.claim: Canonical annotations on HTML pages should be technically unambiguous and should not contradict the final URL identity of priority pages without an intentional consolidation reason.
rules.action: Remove duplicate canonical declarations and review priority HTML URLs that canonicalize away from their final URL.
rules.doesNotProve: That Google will select the declared canonical.

rules.claim: Multiple materially distinct sampled priority HTML URLs collapsing to the same canonical can indicate duplicate routing, generated variants, or accidental loss of page identity.
rules.action: Review duplicate canonical clusters and keep only intentional consolidation.
rules.doesNotProve: Duplicate content or a ranking penalty.

rules.claim: A priority document that exceeds Goose's bounded public fetch budget is not automatically a Search failure, but it deserves retrieval/performance review instead of being misclassified as non-indexable.
rules.action: Review unusually large priority documents and, when practical, keep the landing answer lightweight while moving large datasets/catalog payloads to dedicated retrievable resources.
rules.doesNotProve: That the document exceeds Google's fetch limits, causes a soft 404, or ranks worse because of byte size.

rules.claim: Google describes soft 404s as successful responses that actually present an error, missing-content, empty or nearly empty page.
rules.action: Return meaningful 404/410/redirect status for genuinely missing pages and verify rendered content when a successful page looks empty or error-like.
rules.doesNotProve: That Google has classified the URL as a soft 404.

rules.claim: Important discovery paths should use crawlable anchor elements with real href URLs rather than JavaScript-only or href-less pseudo-links.
rules.action: Replace JavaScript-only or href-less navigation links on important routes with real crawlable anchors where appropriate.
rules.doesNotProve: That every linked URL will be crawled or indexed.

rules.claim: Crawlable internal links on priority pages should resolve to functioning intended targets. Goose samples a bounded set of frequently referenced same-origin targets so broken destinations can be caught without turning Technical Integrity into a whole-site crawler.
rules.action: Fix sampled internal links that resolve to 404/410/5xx targets, and review links that redirect, require authorization, are rate-limited, or cannot be probed reliably.
rules.doesNotProve: That unsampled links are healthy, that a redirect is harmful, or that fixing a broken internal target changes rankings.

rules.claim: Important content should be available in textual form and reliably renderable; extremely thin raw HTML with a script-heavy shell is a technical risk that needs rendered-page review.
rules.action: Ensure critical answer/content exists in reliable rendered text and verify JavaScript-dependent pages with provider/browser tools.
rules.doesNotProve: That raw-HTML text quantity is a ranking factor.

rules.claim: When hreflang is used, language variants should form consistent self-referential and reciprocal clusters.
rules.action: Fix missing self references, malformed alternate URLs, and broken reciprocity inside sampled localization clusters.
rules.doesNotProve: That Google will serve a particular locale URL for every query.

rules.claim: Bing documents that NOSNIPPET/DATA-NOSNIPPET may limit Copilot citation quality, while NOARCHIVE and NOCACHE can restrict use in Copilot or grounding experiences.
rules.action: Review Bing preview/grounding controls on pages intended for Microsoft AI citation and grounding.
rules.doesNotProve: Citation or answer inclusion in Microsoft AI experiences.

rules.claim: Near-identical priority pages can signal route duplication or scaled template expansion that should be reviewed before further indexable growth.
rules.action: Consolidate or materially differentiate near-duplicate priority pages when they do not serve distinct user jobs.
rules.doesNotProve: Spam, a penalty, or lack of user value.

rules.claim: OpenAI says OAI-SearchBot access is relevant to inclusion in ChatGPT summaries/snippets and is separate from GPTBot training controls.
rules.action: Keep OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot policies separate and avoid accidentally blocking OAI-SearchBot when ChatGPT Search discovery is desired.
rules.doesNotProve: ChatGPT citation, ranking, or referral traffic.
